channel.title: Lumen
channel.description: Breakthroughs brought to light. Evidence-first health and medical-technology journalism.

item.title: A twice-yearly shot cut new HIV infections to near zero in trials, and is now reaching Africa.
item.description: Twice-yearly lenacapavir prevented nearly all HIV infections in two large trials zero among 2,134 women in one and a version given every six months won FDA approval in 2025.

item.title: A GLP-1 drug slowed biological-aging markers in the first randomized human evidence.
item.description: Semaglutide slowed multiple DNA-based "aging clocks" by up to ~5 epigenetic years on one measure in the first randomized human evidence, but from a post-hoc analysis in adults with HIV.

item.title: The first FDA-approved gene therapy for inherited deafness improved hearing in most treated children
item.description: The FDA granted accelerated approval to the first gene therapy for inherited deafness; in its trial, 80% of 20 evaluable children gained hearing a result not seen in this condition untreated.

item.title: A new brain stimulation therapy matched ECT for severe depression with less memory loss
item.description: About 48% of patients with severe depression responded to magnetic seizure therapy non-inferior to ECT in the first large head-to-head trial, but with substantially less memory impairment.

item.title: 84% of patients on a weekly survodutide shot cut liver fat in a phase 3 trial
item.description: In a phase 3 trial, 84% of patients on weekly survodutide reduced liver fat by at least 30% vs 24% on placebo though the trial measured liver fat, not long-term liver outcomes.

item.title: Tracked from 70 to 100: a simple "intrinsic capacity" score predicted who survived longest

item.title: Scientists found a hidden T-cell "brake" called SLAMF6 — and antibodies that release it
item.description: Canadian scientists identified SLAMF6, an internal "brake" that exhausts cancer-fighting T cells on its own, and built antibodies to release it — boosting tumor attacks in mice.

item.title: 1 protein switched off made CAR-T cells fight tumors longer — a possible fix for solid cancers
item.description: Disabling a single protein, NFIL3, kept CAR-T cells fighting longer and controlled tumors better in mice, pointing to a possible fix for the solid cancers the therapy has struggled to treat.

item.title: An AI-designed universal coronavirus vaccine just passed its first human trial
item.description: The Cambridge-built shot triggered immune responses against SARS-CoV-2, SARS and bat viruses that haven't yet infected people — aiming to work even as the virus mutates.

item.title: A single nutrient reversed signs of cellular aging — and it's already in your food.
item.description: A nutrient found in everyday food reversed signs of cellular aging within two days, restoring youthful mitochondrial energy in aging cells, German researchers reported.

item.title: 20 years of work yields a compound that blocks a new Alzheimer's target and extends lifespan in mice
item.description: A new compound slowed brain-cell death and extended lifespan in mice by blocking GRK2, an enzyme behind Alzheimer's that existing drugs don't target, ETH Zurich scientists found.

item.title: The child who can now hold a conversation she was born unable to have
item.description: A single gene-therapy injection restored measurable hearing in five of six children born deaf from an OTOF mutation — and two of them can now hold a conversation.

item.title: An AI spotted pancreatic cancer three years before diagnosis — on scans doctors had called normal
item.description: Trained on 24,000 CT scans, an AI flagged pancreatic cancer a mean of three years before clinical diagnosis — on scans that radiologists had reviewed at the time and judged normal.

item.title: Synthetic mRNA told a damaged heart to repair itself — the first human signal that it works
item.description: In a 24-patient Phase 2a trial, an mRNA molecule injected into damaged heart muscle improved the heart's pumping function at three months — the first human evidence that mRNA can trigger cardiac repai

item.title: The swallowable camera that made the colonoscopy optional
item.description: A 968-patient head-to-head trial found the PillCam Colon 2 capsule caught 88% of significant polyps with no sedation and no proceduralist — now FDA-approved for people who skip colonoscopy.
